name: JW Marriott Bali Ubud Resort & Spa
short_description: A luxury JW Marriott resort in Payangan, north of central Ubud, set along the Ayung River valley with jungle-view rooms and villas.
ai_summary: JW Marriott Bali Ubud Resort & Spa sits in Payangan, north of Ubud's town center, positioned along the Ayung River valley in a more remote, jungle-immersed part of the Ubud region than most of Bali's other Bonvoy hotels. Guest feedback is more mixed than at many other properties in this directory, with a rating of 3 of 5 on TripAdvisor within a small, largely luxury-tier hotel field in Payangan. Positive reviews describe the setting as brilliant, with guests praising the pool, surrounding scenery, massage and meditation offerings, and staff who are called friendly, polite, and hospitable, alongside breakfast and food quality that are specifically praised. Given the more limited and mixed review base compared with Bali's more established Bonvoy resorts, this profile reflects a more cautious reading of guest sentiment. The property's Payangan location, farther from both central Ubud and the airport than most of the island's coastal or town-center hotels, is a genuine trade-off for travelers prioritizing a remote, nature-immersed base. For travelers drawn to the JW Marriott brand and a secluded Ayung River valley setting, it remains an option worth evaluating carefully against Bali's other Ubud-area luxury resorts, several of which carry stronger and larger review bases.

faqs.question: Is JW Marriott Bali Ubud Resort & Spa located in central Ubud?
faqs.answer: No -- it's in Payangan, north of Ubud's town center, set along the Ayung River valley in a more remote, jungle-immersed location than most of Bali's other Bonvoy hotels, which means a longer drive to reach central Ubud's shops and restaurants.

faqs.question: How do guests rate JW Marriott Bali Ubud Resort & Spa?
faqs.answer: It carries a 3-of-5 rating on TripAdvisor, more mixed than several other Bali Bonvoy properties, though guests consistently praise the pool, scenery, staff friendliness, and food quality, so it's worth weighing against Ubud's other, more established resorts.
